name: Hippius
own_description: Blockchain-backed cloud: storage, VMs, and apps with unmatched transparency, trust, and power.

paragraphs: A Hippius storage miner keeps pieces of users’ files online, serves them and answers challenges that prove it still holds them. Your subnet 75 hotkey, the key you work with as a miner, identifies your Hippius family account. The family must register on Hippius, which can charge a variable family registration fee, and each storage node needs a child account and a signature from its node key. With slot lockup enabled, the default is one lifetime deposit-free slot per family, and a paid slot takes a variable deposit that the family can reclaim about seven days after the child deregisters. With lockup off, no deposit is required.

The code combines recent reports across active family nodes, and data served counts for 70% while data stored counts for 30%, with diminishing returns on both. New families with a positive raw score get a minimum raw weight of 10 through scoring-bucket age 24, inclusive. The Bittensor weight calculation budgets 1% for storage miners by family weight and 99% for UID 238. Hippius separately pays storage emissions in hALPHA to eligible families by raw score, excluding the account associated with UID 238. Hippius rankings use six-hour eras, and Arion checks for storage payments every 14,400 blocks, about 24 hours.

Splitting the same bytes across more nodes leaves the base score unchanged. Downtime reduces the score, and the code averages penalties for strikes and integrity failures across contributing nodes. Deregistering a child forfeits that node’s unpaid storage accruals. Read from https://github.com/thenervelab/thebrain at commit 2eb6561 on 2026-11-23.
mining_note.how_it_was_made: This note was put together by AI agents and not by a person who mines here. One agent read the subnet's public repository and wrote down what a miner does, what it takes and how the work is paid, with a source for each statement, and a second agent opened every source and took out whatever it did not support. Of 30 source checks, 15 held, 1 did not hold and 14 could not be opened, and only what held is in the text above. Nothing of the subnet's code was run, and the note describes the code as it stood on the day and at the commit named in its last sentence, so it can be out of date.
